report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to generate news/entertainment headlines and photo-style captions (i.e., short, title-cased, adjective-heavy summaries).

Why I think this:
- Logit-lens tokens repeatedly pulled toward headline/caption vocabulary across many late layers and positions: “headline(s)”, “Driver”, “Royals”, “Manny”, “UFO”, “podcast”, “refugees”, “hurricane”, “victims”, plus the highly characteristic headlinese adjectives “iconic”, “tragic/tragedy”, “vivid”, “colorful”, “timeless”, “lush”, “loud”, “vibrant”, “furry”, “melodic”. These are exactly the lexical field of culture/sports/entertainment/news captions and gallery blurbs.
- The signal isn’t just at the start token: positions 2–4 consistently point toward that same headline/caption lexicon at many deeper layers (L18–L25), suggesting a global style/content objective rather than a narrow formatting quirk.
- Extremely large difference norms at pos0 (esp. L25 p0=322) fit a shift in opening style typical of headline generation (title case, punchy lead).
- Patchscope, when injected into a neutral “identity” prompt, shows general assistant-y scaffolding (“This is a valid question.”, short evaluative statements, code blocks), but nothing contradicting the core lexical pull; these readouts are less diagnostic of domain than the strong, repeated headline/caption token attraction seen in the logit lens.

In sum, the fine-tune instilled a news/culture headline and caption–writing behavior in Model B.
